property_summary: For any caller, the reference contract's owner() always returns the stored owner address (the account set at initialization), whereas the mutant returns msg.sender so it can return different addresses depending on the caller.

For any caller address, the reference contract's owner() always returns the stored owner (the address set at initialization), whereas the mutant returns msg.sender so owner() can differ when called by different callers.

For all callers, the correct contract C returns the same stored owner address (the initializer-set owner) from owner(); the mutant returns msg.sender so there exists a caller for which owner() differs, causing a mismatch between owner() called by that caller and the stored owner getter behavior.
For any contract state, paused() returns the actual stored paused flag; the mutant inverts that value (returns !paused) and thus disagrees for states where the stored flag is true or false.

For every input, the reference contract's paused() returns the actual stored paused flag; the mutant inverts the stored flag so there exist inputs (calls after pause/unpause) where paused() differs, so the property is: paused() equals the boolean stored by calling pause()/unPause() sequence — reference satisfies for all sequences, mutant fails for some.

For every sequence of pause/unpause calls, C.paused() returns the actual stored paused flag (true after pause(), false after unPause()); the mutant inverts the stored flag so there exist calls where paused() differs.

After any single call to pause() or unPause(), the public paused() getter returns true iff pause() was called most recently (i.e., paused() reflects the last action); the mutant inverts the stored flag and will return the opposite for some fuzzed sequences.

For any sequence where a caller (fuzzed actor) calls either pause() or unPause() exactly once, the public paused() view must reflect the actual stored paused flag (true after pause(), false after unPause()); the mutant inverts the stored flag and therefore will return the opposite for some fuzzed actor sequences.

For any tokenId and after initialization, if no per-token royalty recipient is set (stored recipient == address(0)), getRoyalties must return the global royaltyRecipient with royaltyBPS == 500; the mutant wrongly returns royaltyBPS == 1000 for such tokens.

For any tokenId after initialize, if no per-token royalty recipient has been set (stored recipient == address(0)), getRoyalties must return the global royaltyRecipient with royaltyBPS == 500; the mutant returns 1000 for such tokens and thus violates this rule for some tokenId.

For any tokenId after initialize, if the stored per-token royalty recipient is the zero address, getRoyalties(tokenId) must return the global royaltyRecipient and royaltyBPS == 500; the mutant returns royaltyBPS == 1000 for such tokenIds, violating this rule for some inputs.

For any tokenId after initialize, if no per-token royalty recipient has been configured (stored recipient == address(0)), getRoyalties(tokenId) returns the global royaltyRecipient with royaltyBPS == 500; the mutant returns royaltyBPS == 1000 for such tokenIds, violating this rule for some inputs.

For any tokenId after initialize, if the stored per-token royalty recipient is address(0) (i.e. no per-token override), getRoyalties(tokenId) MUST return the contract-level royaltyRecipient with royaltyBPS == 500; the mutant returns royaltyBPS == 1000 for such tokenIds and thus violates this rule for some tokenId inputs.

If the contract has not been initialized (initializeRoyalties not called), calling getRoyalties must revert (reference) — the mutant instead returns a default zeroed RoyaltyConfiguration for some tokenId, breaking the rule.

For any tokenId, if no per-token override is set then getRoyalties returns the stored default royaltyRecipient with royaltyBPS == 500; the mutant returns royaltyBPS == 0 for such tokens, violating this invariant for some tokenId.
For every tokenId, the reference returns a non-zero default royaltyBPS (500) when no per-token royaltyRecipient is set; the mutant returns 0 BPS for some tokenId (breaking this invariant).
